item.description:
Vespers, Sunday evenings at 5:00 PM | In person only A contemplative candlelit service to nurture mind, body and spirit Join us Sunday evenings for Vespers, a warm and inviting weekly gathering in the serene surroundings of the Saint James Chapel. This quiet, reflective service embraces Christianity’s rich prayer traditions and the embodied practices that nurture our spiritual lives today. Gather with us for uplifting singing, find solace in moments of silence, and choose the posture that feels most comfortable as we open our hearts to listen for God’s voice and center ourselves for the week ahead. item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Nov 11, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.
Cost: Free Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult) When: Every

item.title: First Friday Compline, All Saints — Fri Nov 6, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description: All Saints, All Souls The names of all the recently departed we have prayed for in the Prayers of the People, as well as the names of those who have died in the past year and were submitted to the church, will be read aloud. These readings of names and the remembering of our dead of this past year in these special services allow us to create sacred and holy worship experiences that hold together the range of feelings that are part of that first year of losing a loved one. The sheer grief we feel with the loss of their presence in our daily lives, the grief of a relationship that may not have ended as we had hoped, and the myriad ways that grief ebbs and flows as we find a new way of being in the world. item.title: Children's Chapel — Sun Nov 8, 10:30 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Nov 3, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Nov 3, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
